transcript:
YOU
Use inspectGeoDataset on the attached GeoTIFF and report its size, coordinate reference system, bands and any data-quality concerns. The band order is 1=blue, 2=green, 3=red, 4=near-infrared. Then use computeBandMath for a normalized-difference NDVI with bandA=4 and bandB=3.
PAPYRUS
I'll inspect the raster and then run the NDVI band math.
◫ Raster inspector ↗
PAPYRUS
◫ Raster inspector ↗
PAPYRUS
GeoTIFF Inspection
Source: /Library/Sessions/160b3dc2…/Library/Uploads/05c97ee5…-sentinel2-salinas-2025-09-22-blue-green-red-nir.tif (sha256 05c97ee51867…)
Size and coverage
PROPERTY	VALUE
Raster size	728 × 680 px (495,040 px total)
Format	GeoTIFF, tiled/striped (GeoTIFF.js windowed preview)
CRS	EPSG:32610 — WGS 84 / UTM zone 10N
Bounds	E 660,620 – 667,900; N 4,065,320 – 4,072,120 (UTM 10N metres)
Ground extent	≈ 7.28 km × 6.80 km; ≈ 10 m/px ground sample distance (consistent with Sentinel-2 at native resolution)
Location	UTM 10N easting/northing places this in central California — consistent with the Salinas Valley in the filename
Bands (4), as declared 1=blue, 2=green, 3=red, 4=near-infrared
Statistics below come from the 2,160-pixel sampled preview, not the full raster:
BAND	MIN	MAX	MEAN	CHARACTER
1 — blue	179	1,354	653.1	Lowest signal, lowest dynamic range
2 — green	287	1,974	967.3	Moderate
3 — red	261	3,064	1,483.3	High
4 — NIR	740	4,328	2,335.3	Highest overall, as expected for vegetation
Band 4 having the highest mean and band 1 the lowest is physically consistent with the declared ordering — a useful sanity check that the band order matches the file.
Data-quality concerns
No nodata mask reported. The tool returned no nodata value and no zero-count. Band minimums are all well above zero (179–740), which is unusual for raw Sentinel-2 DN and suggests the file was already scaled/offset or contrast-stretched before upload. You cannot treat these values as calibrated reflectance or as raw DN without the processing history.
Statistics are sampled, not full-raster. The tool is explicit: "Statistics describe sampled preview pixels, not the full raster." Min/max/mean are from 2,160 pixels and are not global. True extremes and the real distribution are unverified.
No explicit units. No scale/offset or unit metadata was surfaced, so the band values are unitless as reported here.
No cloud, shadow, or water mask. A date of 2025-09-22 for an agricultural area gives no assurance about cloud cover or field-level artifacts; nothing in the metadata lets me confirm or rule that out.
Extremes may be contamination, not signal. The NDVI maximum of 0.817 (see below) is likely genuine dense vegetation, but the extremes in the red band (max 3,064) are worth checking against a full-raster histogram before drawing conclusions.
CRS is projected, not geographic. Distances and areas in this raster are in UTM metres; do not mix with lat/lon without reprojection. No reprojection was performed.
NDVI — normalized difference, bandA=4 (NIR), bandB=3 (red)
Formula applied: (band 4 − band 3) / (band 4 + band 3). Sampled over the same 2,160-pixel preview.
STATISTIC	VALUE
Min	0.0508
Max	0.8168
Mean	0.2265
Sample count	2,160
Reading the result: every sampled pixel is positive, so NIR exceeds red across the whole preview. The mean of 0.2265 is a low-to-moderate vegetation signal — more consistent with sparse or early-stage canopy, bare soil with partial cover, or a mixed agricultural scene than with a fully closed crop canopy (which would typically sit well above 0.5 on average). The bulk of the preview falls in a tight band between roughly 0.13 and 0.30, with a modest tail of high values (0.4–0.8) where dense vegetation is present.
Caveats on this number:
Sampled preview, not full raster — the reported min/max/mean are not global statistics.
Zero denominators yield no value; none were flagged here, but the tool reports NaN counts only where they occur.
Per instruction, this is descriptive output only. I have not converted NDVI into vegetation fraction, biomass, crop type, or any agronomic interpretation, and no field boundaries or labels were applied.
Both operations were read-only; nothing was written or modified. If you want global (full-raster) statistics rather than sampled preview values, or a written GeoTIFF of the NDVI, tell me and I'll look for the appropriate raster path.
Done
